FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A60
Do not follow emergency fire apparatus closer than five hundred feet or enter or park within the block where it has stopped for an emergency. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A60
Yield to a funeral-procession escort vehicle displaying the required audible or visible emergency signals. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A60
Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, reduce speed and be ready to stop. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A60
The manual calls for a safe clearance of at least three feet from a pedestrian on a roadway. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A60
Stop for a white-cane or guide-dog user and wait until the person is well beyond the roadway or your vehicle's path. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A60
Follow a police officer's directions when the officer is controlling traffic. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A60
Nebraska's basic speed rule requires a reasonable, safe speed for the conditions that exist. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A60
Unless a sign states otherwise, the handbook's business-district maximum is twenty miles per hour. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A60
The printed unposted residential-district maximum is twenty-five miles per hour. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A60
The printed unposted maximum on gravel or another nondustless road is fifty miles per hour. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A60
The printed unposted maximum on a dustless or paved road outside the state highway system is fifty-five miles per hour. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A60
The printed unposted maximum on a four-lane divided highway outside the state system is sixty-five miles per hour. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A60
The printed unposted state-highway maximum is sixty-five miles per hour when the road is not an expressway, super-two highway or freeway. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A60
For state-system expressways, super-two highways and freeways, the printed unposted maximum is seventy miles per hour, with rural interstate highways separately listed at seventy-five. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A60
The manual separately lists seventy-five miles per hour on rural interstates unless posted otherwise. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A60
Watch posted speed signs rather than assuming that the default roadway category applies. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A60
Generally keep pace with the main traffic stream to limit repeated passing and allow adjustment to slower vehicles. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A60
Below-normal-speed traffic uses the right available lane except when passing same-direction traffic or preparing for an intersection, private-road or driveway left turn. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A61
Do not unnecessarily obstruct normal reasonable traffic flow; safety, emergencies or law can require a slower speed. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A61
In work zones, remain alert, follow controls, keep a steady traffic-consistent speed unless directed differently, and allow for restricted maneuvering space. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A61
In a work zone, position away from workers and equipment, avoid sudden slowing and remain prepared to stop. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A61
In school zones, slow down, obey signs and remain ready to stop. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A61
The manual doubles fines in school zones and in work zones when workers are present. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> pdf-0061]

Misconceptions: Keeping pace with traffic does not create permission to exceed a posted limit; a passing maneuver still has speed and visibility constraints.
Mnemonics: Choose a safe lawful speed, identify the passing restriction, preserve space.
Glossary: A dustless roadway includes a paved road; a posted limit can replace a default category; advisory speed is distinct from the legal maximum.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.
